extracted.intended_audience: national intellectual property / patent offices, WIPO/International Bureau staff, government agents, patent attorneys and policy makers implementing or applying the International Patent Classification
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards establishing the International Patent Classification (IPC) Special Union: its composition, use of the Classification, language and publication rules, amendment and revision procedures, governance (Assembly, Committee of Experts, International Bureau), finances, accession and denunciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of Special Union and adoption of a common classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 1 — The countries to which this Agreement applies constitute a Special Union and adopt a common classification for patents for invention, inventors' certificates, utility models and utility certificates, to be known as the 'International Patent Classification' (the 'Classification').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates the legal basis obliging parties to be members of the Special Union and to use/adopt the common IPC; frames the Classification as the foundational instrument for international cooperation in patent classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and contents of the Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 2(1)(a)-(b) — The Classification comprises: (i) the text established pursuant to the European Convention (Dec 19, 1954) as published; (ii) amendments entered into force pursuant to article 2(2) of the European Convention prior to entry into force of this Agreement; (iii) amendments made thereafter in accordance with Article 5 which enter into force pursuant to Article 6. The Guide and the notes included in the text of the Classification are an integral part thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what textual materials constitute the authoritative Classification (original text, Guide/notes, and amendments) and how amendments become part of the Classification; establishes authenticity and continuity with the European Convention texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposition of authentic copies and amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 2(2)-(6) — The original text and certain amendments must be deposited in two authentic copies (English and French) with the Secretary General of the Council of Europe and the Director General of WIPO; later amendments are deposited in one authentic copy with the Director General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets custody and authentication rules for authoritative texts and for deposit of amendments to ensure availability of authentic versions in English and French.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages of the Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 3 — The Classification shall be established in the English and French languages, both texts being equally authentic. Official texts in German, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish and other languages may be established by the International Bureau in consultation with interested Governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates English/French as equally authentic originals and authorizes the International Bureau to produce official translations in other languages after consultation, with attention to budgetary implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative character and allowable uses of the Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 4(1)-(2) — The Classification shall be solely of an administrative character. Each country of the Special Union shall have the right to use the Classification either as a principal or as a subsidiary system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that the IPC is an administrative tool (not substantive law) and allows states flexibility to adopt it as primary or secondary classification according to national practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to include complete IPC symbols in documents and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 4(3) — The competent authorities of the countries of the Special Union shall include in patents, inventors' certificates, utility models and utility certificates issued by them, and in applications relating thereto (published or laid open for public inspection), and in notices appearing in official periodicals, the complete symbols of the Classification applied to the invention to which the document relates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires inclusion of full IPC symbols in patent documents and official publication notices to promote uniformity and retrievability of classified documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservations on inclusion of group/subgroup symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 4(4) — At signature or deposit of instrument of ratification or accession, any country may declare that it does not undertake to include symbols relating to groups or subgroups in applications only laid open for public inspection and related notices; any country that does not proceed to an examination as to novelty and whose grant procedure does not provide for a search into the state of the art may declare that it does not undertake to include the symbols relating to groups and subgroups in the documents and notices referred to in paragraph (3); if limited to certain protections or fields, reservation may be limited accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives countries a formal, limited reservation right where practical or procedural reasons (e.g., no novelty examination or certain technologies) make inclusion of fine-grained symbols impracticable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and presentation of IPC symbols in documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 4(5) — The symbols of the Classification, preceded by the words 'International Patent Classification' or an abbreviation to be determined by the Committee of Experts, shall be printed in heavy type, or in such a manner that they are clearly visible, in the heading of each document in which they are to be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes conspicuous presentation of IPC symbols (label + heavy type/clear visibility) in document headings to ensure clarity and consistent appearance across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Classification by intergovernmental authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 4(6) — If any country entrusts the grant of patents to an intergovernmental authority, it shall take all possible measures to ensure that this authority uses the Classification in accordance with this Article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends the obligation to ensure use of the Classification to cases where patent-granting is delegated to intergovernmental bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment, composition and representation in the Committee of Experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 5(1)-(2) — A Committee of Experts shall be set up in which each country of the Special Union shall be represented. The Director General shall invite intergovernmental organizations specialized in the patent field to be represented by observers; other organizations may be invited to participate in discussions of interest to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates the central expert body for IPC maintenance, with state representation and formal observer participation by relevant intergovernmental/international organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of the Committee of Experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 5(3) — The Committee of Experts shall: (i) Amend the Classification; (ii) Address recommendations to facilitate the use and promote uniform application; (iii) Assist in promotion of international cooperation in reclassification of documentation used for examination, taking needs of developing countries into account; (iv) Take measures (without financial implications for the Special Union/Organization) to facilitate application by developing countries; (v) Have the right to establish subcommittees and working groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies operational remit: amendment authority, promotion of uniformity and assistance especially for developing countries, and ability to form substructures for specialized work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal submission and notice requirements for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 5(5) — Proposals for amendments to the Classification may be made by the competent authority of any country of the Special Union, the International Bureau, any intergovernmental organization represented in the Committee and any other organization specially invited; proposals shall be communicated to the International Bureau which shall submit them to Committee members and observers not later than two months before the Committee session at which they are to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes who may propose amendments and requires at least two months' advance circulation to Committee members/observers to allow consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting and decision thresholds in the Committee of Experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 5(6) — Each country member of the Committee shall have one vote. Decisions require a simple majority of countries represented and voting. Any decision regarded by one-fifth of countries represented and voting as giving rise to a modification in the basic structure of the Classification or entailing substantial reclassification shall require a majority of three-fourths. Abstentions are not considered votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines voting equality (one state = one vote) and special supermajority protection for fundamental or burdensome changes; abstentions excluded from denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification, entry into force and publication of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 6(1)-(2) — Every decision of the Committee concerning adoption of amendments and recommendations shall be notified by the International Bureau to competent authorities; amendments enter into force six months from date of dispatch of notification. The International Bureau shall incorporate amendments which have entered into force into the Classification and publish announcements in periodicals designated by the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a six-month lead time between notification and entry into force and obligations on the International Bureau to incorporate and publish amendments for transparency and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly composition, delegation and observers
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 7(1) — The Special Union shall have an Assembly consisting of the countries of the Special Union; each Government shall be represented by one delegate, who may be assisted by alternates, advisors and experts. Any intergovernmental organization referred to in Article 5(2)(a) may be represented by an observer, and, if the Assembly decides, in committees or working groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes governing plenary body with equal state representation and possible observer participation by relevant organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers and duties of the Assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 7(2)(a) — Subject to Article 5, the Assembly shall: (i) Deal with all matters concerning maintenance/development of the Special Union and implementation of this Agreement; (ii) Give directions to the International Bureau concerning preparation for revision conferences; (iii) Review and approve reports/activities of the Director General concerning the Special Union; (iv) Determine program and adopt triennial budget and approve final accounts; (v) Adopt financial regulations; (vi) Decide establishment of official texts in other languages; (vii) Establish committees/working groups; (viii) Determine observers to be admitted; (ix) Take other actions to further objectives; (x) Perform other appropriate functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive enumerated powers including governance, budgetary control, language/text decisions, and organizational arrangements; Assembly may take broad actions to further the Special Union's objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly voting, quorum and procedural rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 7(3)-(5) — Each country member of the Assembly shall have one vote. One-half of the members constitute a quorum. In absence of quorum the Assembly may make decisions which take effect only if later confirmed by absent members within three months to attain the required quorum and majority. Decisions of the Assembly shall require two-thirds of the votes cast (subject to Article 11(2)). Abstentions are not considered votes. The Assembly shall meet once every third calendar year in ordinary session and may meet in extraordinary session upon request of one-fourth of the countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies thresholds (one vote per state, half for quorum, two-thirds for decisions), quorum fallback procedure by written votes, meeting frequency and convocation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau administrative tasks and Director General role
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 8(1)-(4) — Administrative tasks concerning the Special Union shall be performed by the International Bureau. It shall prepare meetings and provide secretariat of the Assembly, Committee of Experts and other committees; the Director General shall be chief executive of the Special Union and represent it. The Director General and designated staff participate without vote in all meetings and act as ex officio secretaries. The International Bureau shall prepare for revision conferences and carry out any other tasks assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designates the International Bureau as the operational secretariat and the Director General as executive, with defined participatory (non-voting) and preparatory responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finances: budget composition, contributions and arrears
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 9(1)-(4) — The Special Union shall have a budget including income/expenses proper to the Special Union, contribution to common expenses and sums for the Organization's Conference. The budget shall be financed from: (i) contributions of countries of the Special Union; (ii) fees/charges for services by the International Bureau; (iii) sale/royalties on publications; (iv) gifts, bequests and subventions; (v) rents, interests and miscellaneous income. Each country belongs to the same class as in the Paris Union and pays annual contribution on the same unit basis; contributions become due on 1 January. A country in arrears equal to or exceeding contributions due for the preceding two full years may be deprived of its right to vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lays out multiple funding streams, formula for apportioning contributions tied to Paris Union classes, due dates, and punitive treatment for arrears while allowing exceptions for exceptional unavoidable circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working capital fund and auditing
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 9(6)-(8) — The Special Union shall have a working capital fund constituted by a single payment by each country; if insufficient, the Assembly shall decide to increase it with proportions fixed by the Assembly on proposal of the Director General. Auditing of the accounts shall be effected by one or more of the countries of the Special Union or by external auditors as provided in financial regulations and designated by the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes working capital funding mechanism, rules for increases and auditing procedures to ensure financial accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision of the Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 10 — The Agreement may be revised from time to time by a special conference of the countries of the Special Union; convocation of any revision conference shall be decided by the Assembly. Articles 7, 8, 9 and 11 may be amended either by a revision conference or according to Article 11 provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides formal route for substantive changes to the Agreement via revision conferences called by the Assembly; specifies certain articles that have specific amendment routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment procedure for specified articles and entry into force of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 11(1)-(3) — Proposals to amend Articles 7, 8, 9 and this Article may be initiated by any country or by the Director General and must be communicated at least six months in advance to Assembly consideration. Amendments shall be adopted by the Assembly requiring three-fourths of votes cast (and four-fifths for amendments to Article 7 and the present paragraph). Any amendment to these articles enters into force one month after written notifications of acceptance have been received by the Director General from three-fourths of countries of the Special Union at the time the amendment was adopted. Amendments thus accepted bind all countries which are members at entry into force; amendments increasing financial obligations bind only countries which have notified acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines higher thresholds (3/4 or 4/5) and timing/notification requirements for amendments to core governance/financial provisions and how binding effect is allocated, especially for financial obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming a party (accession/ratification) and deposit of instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 12 — Any country party to the Paris Convention may become party to this Agreement by signature followed by deposit of an instrument of ratification or by deposit of an instrument of accession. Instruments shall be deposited with the Director General. The provisions of Article 24 of the Stockholm Act of the Paris Convention shall apply to this Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits eligibility for accession to Paris Convention parties and centralizes depositary functions with the Director General of WIPO; cross-references Stockholm Act procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force of the Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 13(1)-(2) — The Agreement shall enter into force one year after instruments of ratification or accession have been deposited by: (i) two-thirds of the countries party to the European Convention on the date on which this Agreement is opened for signature; and (ii) three countries party to the Paris Convention not previously party to the European Convention, of which at least one is a country where, according to recent statistics, more than 40,000 patent applications have been filed. For other countries, the Agreement enters into force one year after notification of deposit by the Director General (unless a subsequent date indicated). Ratification or accession entails acceptance of all clauses and admission to all advantages of this Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies compound threshold conditions for initial entry into force (reflecting European Convention and Paris Convention participant mix and inclusion of major filer requirement) and standard one-year lag for subsequent accessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of the Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 14 — This Agreement shall have the same duration as the Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synchronizes the Agreement's temporal scope with the Paris Convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denunciation (withdrawal) procedure and timing restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 15 — Any country may denounce this Agreement by notification to the Director General. Denunciation shall take effect one year after the Director General has received the notification. The right of denunciation shall not be exercised before the expiration of five years from the date upon which a country becomes a member of the Special Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines formal withdrawal process, one-year notice period, and a five-year minimum membership period before denunciation may be exercised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature, authentic texts, transmission, depositary and notification duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 16(1)-(5) — The Agreement shall be signed in a single original in English and French (both equally authentic). It shall remain open for signature at Strasbourg until Sept 30, 1971. The original when no longer open shall be deposited with the Director General. Official texts to be established in other languages by the Director General after consultation. The Director General shall transmit certified copies of the signed text and of any amendment to Governments and to the Secretary General of the Council of Europe, furnish certified copies of the Classification on request, register the Agreement with the UN Secretariat, and notify Governments of signatures, deposits of instruments, entry into force, reservations, acceptances of amendments, dates of entry into force of amendments and denunciations received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies authentication in English/French, depositary role of the Director General, procedures for producing/transmitting certified copies, UN registration and extensive notification duties for transparency and record-keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional provisions for European Convention parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 17(1)-(3) — During two years following entry into force, countries party to the European Convention which are not yet members of the Special Union may enjoy the same rights in the Committee of Experts as if they were members. During three years following that two-year period they may be represented by observers in Committee meetings and, if Committee so decides, in subcommittees or working groups; they may submit proposals for amendments and shall be notified of Committee decisions/recommendations. During five years following entry into force they may be represented by observers in meetings of the Assembly and, if Assembly decides, in committees or working groups established by it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides phased transitional participation and proposal/notification rights for European Convention parties not yet members of the Special Union to facilitate continuity and gradual integration.
